items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: “Hal, I need a first trumpet player because Don Smith, my regular trumpet player, is on staff at NBC and we’re taking a tour through the south and I’d like you to be my first chair player and when we come back it’s your job.

ctx.x: Buddy Childers. Yes, God. He was another like brother to me. I didn’t know him, I knew of him in high school looking at the back of Stan Kenton albums. So he was having problems in Vegas because of his attitude and he was burning every bridge he was at. So he was there in Vegas not being able to work and I had my tonsils to get out so I called

Buddy to see if he could take my place for a week. He did and he just really thanked me because I helped him when he was in a down part of his life. And then he moved to L.A. He said, “When you come into L.A. call me.” So I did maybe a year later and he remembered — he took me with him to dates because he had burned his bridge the first time around with all his contractor friends. When he came back the second time he was okay with it and started working. And I got a phone call from Butch Stone. He was the…

And the military always gave us their hats, you know, Squad 47 or whatever the names. I’ve got a collection of these caps in the garage that I kept all these years. But you know the troops, when we were through playing and performing, they’d come up to the band and thank us so much for being there, you know leaving home over Christmas to entertain them. And I thought then you know even if I didn’t get paid I’d want to do this, just because of how I felt doing it.
